facts.statement: Phosphatotitan lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian in the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis.
facts.quote: The type species is P. khouribgaensis.

facts.statement: Phosphatotitan was described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Nicholas R. Longrich and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2026, Nicholas R. Longrich and colleagues described Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis as a new genus and species

facts.statement: A dorsal vertebral centrum of Phosphatotitan measures 15.9 cm in height, about 39.75 % of the size of Patagotitan.
facts.quote: With a dorsal vertebral centrum height of 15.9 cm, the linear dimensions of the Phosphatotitan fossils are about 39.75% of those of Patagotitan.

facts.statement: Phosphatotitan is estimated to have weighed between 3.5 and 4.3 tonnes, roughly 6.3 % of Patagotitan’s mass.
facts.quote: its weight can be calculated to be between 3.5 and 4.3 t, around 6.3% of the mass of Patagotitan.

facts.statement: Other dinosaurs known from the same deposits include hadrosaurids Ajnabia, Minqaria, Taleta and the abelisaurid theropod Chenanisaurus.
facts.quote: include diverse hadrosaurids, including Ajnabia, Minqaria, and Taleta, in addition to the abelisaurid theropod Chenanisaurus

facts.statement: Phosphatotitan’s temporal range is Maastrichtian, from about 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Phosphatotitan is recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
